subject: Postpay telemetry gaps — proposed interim credit for missing tokens
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@acmeind.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, ops+billing@acmeind.com
Date: 2027-08-31T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unattributed postpay tokens / telemetry gaps for 8/24-8/30

Hi Soojin / Acme billing team,

We ran our monthly reconciliation and noticed ~1.2M tokens that appear on our Redwoods invoiced usage (postpay) but do not show up in the telemetry export we pulled from your dashboard for 2027-08-24 00:00 — 2027-08-30 23:59 (UTC). The spike correlates with a scheduled batch job on our side, but the request_ids in your telemetry export don't match the token_count in the invoice line items.

We attached a representative sample (acme_usage_sample_0808-0814.csv) and highlighted a few request_ids that are in the billing ledger but not in the telemetry file. This is blocking our finance team from closing the month.

Can Redwood propose an interim credit while you investigate the root cause? If you need additional logs, we can provide server-side timestamps and the job id. Also please confirm the timeline for a final reconciliation and whether this will affect our monthly invoice.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of FinOps, Acme Industries
ops+billing@acmeind.com

Attachment: acme_usage_sample_0808-0814.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acmeind.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unattributed postpay tokens / telemetry gaps for 8/24-8/30

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear sample and the heads up. I've looped in Lauren (billing reconciliation) and Michael (runtime telemetry) so we can triage.

Quick notes and proposed path forward:
- We're seeing a known edge-case where streaming retries (client-side) plus a short telemetry aggregation delay can produce ledger-attributed tokens before telemetry dedup finishes. That can look like "tokens billed but not in export" for a short window.
- We want to propose a provisional (interim) credit to remove the month-close blocker: $4,800 (roughly 1.2M tokens at your agreed postpay rate). If you accept, we'll apply the credit to the Sep invoice and mark it as provisional pending final reconciliation.
- Technical next steps: Michael will request a high-resolution telemetry export (with request_id, trace_id, server_ts, and retry_count) for 8/24–8/30. Lauren will run a preliminary ledger vs telemetry diff and share the method.
- Timeline: provisional credit posted within 2 business days after you sign the attached provisional_credit_agreement_v1.pdf; final reconciliation expected within 10 business days after we receive the full telemetry export. Any true overbilling found will be reversed; any undercount identified on your side will be billed in the next cycle.

Please reply with acceptance of the provisional credit terms and whether we should proceed. If you'd rather wait for the full audit before any adjustment, tell us and we'll prioritize the telemetry export.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128

Attachments: provisional_credit_agreement_v1.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@acmeind.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unattributed postpay tokens / telemetry gaps for 8/24-8/30

Thanks all — adding the preliminary recon methodology here so Acme can review before we run a larger job.

Method summary (prelim_recon_20270831.csv attached):
1) Normalize both feeds to UTC and align to 1-second buckets.
2) Join on request_id first; unmatched ledger rows -> attempt match by trace_id + client_ts window ±5s.
3) Mark rows with retry_count > 0 as potential duplicates; those are excluded from provisional credit unless telemetry shows no successful completion.
4) Any ledger tokens remaining unmatched after step 2 are considered "unattributed" and form the basis for the provisional credit amount.

For transparency we'll include: matched_count, unmatched_count, and the raw evidence rows per unmatched item. If Acme is comfortable, we can run the full diff for 8/24–8/30 tonight and share the CSV. Estimated run-time: 3–4 hours.

Two asks for Acme before we run:
- Provide the job id and server-side timestamps you mentioned so we can line up trace_id heuristics.
- Confirm acceptance of the provisional credit posting to the Sep invoice (we'll label it: "Provisional credit — telemetry investigation")

If accepted, I'll run the full diff and attach the evidence export to the reconciliation ticket.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Billing Specialist, Revenue Ops
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: prelim_recon_20270831.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Maya Patel <maya@acmeind.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unattributed postpay tokens / telemetry gaps for 8/24-8/30

Hi Soojin / Lauren — thanks for the quick triage and the clear methodology. Acme accepts the provisional credit of $4,800 applied to our September invoice while Redwood runs the full reconciliation.

We will:
- Share the job id and server-side timestamps by EOD today (I put the files in the shared Drive link you provided).
- Review the prelim_recon CSV once you post it.

Can you confirm the accounting memo you'll add to the invoice (so our AP team can match it)? Also, please send the provisional_credit_agreement_v1.pdf to our legal procurement contact (agreements@acmeind.com) so they have a signed record.

Thanks — this will help us close the month.

Maya
